name: primitives-animate-code-block

frames.best_why: The whole snippet is written out, showing the finished highlighted code with every line visible.

tagline: Code types itself out inside a dark editor window.
summary: A dark code panel with a filename bar where syntax-highlighted code is written out character by character when it scrolls into view, scrolling down as it grows.
appearance: A dark, rounded editor panel with a header of three grey dots and a small counter.tsx filename. Below it, monospace code appears in syntax colours: purple imports, teal punctuation and olive strings on near-black.
behaviour: When the panel enters the viewport the code is typed one character at a time over a few seconds, the viewport scrolling down to follow the newest line. It stops when the whole snippet has been written.
demo_content: A counter.tsx React example importing useState and rendering a button that counts clicks.
search_phrases: terminal style code reveal on scroll
show code being written character by character
dark code panel with traffic light dots
live coding animation for landing page
use_when: A docs or marketing page should present a code sample with motion that draws the eye.
avoid_when: Typing hides the full snippet for seconds, and the effect needs shiki plus a scroll container to read.
customise: Pass code and lang, pick light or dark themes, and set writing, duration, delay and in-view options; the character interval and auto-scroll are built in.
weight_why: Shiki re-highlights the snippet on every character while typing, then settles once done.

a11y.note: The changing highlighted markup is noisy for screen readers and no reduced-motion check skips the typing.

issues: Early frames show a mostly empty panel with one line, which looks sparse.
There is no blinking caret, so it is hard to see where typing is at a glance.
polish_why: Believable editor chrome and clean syntax colours; long empty stretches while typing.
title: Animated Code Block
